Definition: secure; in a bad sense, haughty
BiblicalUsage: Sha'anan is secure, at ease — and in the bad sense, haughty. Amos cries woe to them that are at ease in Zion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria. And the LORD answers Sennacherib's rage and tumult the same way: I will put My hook in thy nose, and My bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that ease without God is the pride that gets a hook in its nose — Zion at ease and Assyria raging are turned back the same way.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
